title: A spec is written end to end with the lathe command
expected_result: Expects the written data to load with every key and check, and lathe check to pass.

title: Split a product into domains by capability
steps: On a temporary product, reads the modeling skill's first step and the reference's Domain, then adds two domains with their subdomain types through lathe add.
Runs lathe check: the domain titled for a technology is warned of; renames it for its capability with lathe set and checks again.
expected_result: Expects the warning for the technology title only, and none after the rename.

title: Change the schema with a migration
steps: In a copy of the lathe package, writes the next numbered migration adding a column to term.
Runs the schema and reference scripts there, then adds a term with the new column and runs lathe check on a temporary product.
expected_result: Expects the row types and reference stale before and current after, the copy to accept and check the new column, and the unchanged Lathe to refuse it.

title: Declare a product's own kind and relation
steps: On a temporary product, declares a product kind with a field and a new relation through the MCP add tool.
Adds a record of the new kind and a link of the new relation through lathe; declares the kind again through lathe and in the data file.
expected_result: Expects the server to announce its tools again with the new table, the record and link written, and the second declaration refused naming the file and line.

title: Organize use cases into capabilities and a pattern
steps: On a temporary product, adds a capability, moves a use case under it and writes a pattern with a setting and a rule.
Links two use cases to the pattern, answers one setting, checks, then answers the other.
expected_result: Expects a repeated position, an upper-case setting and an unknown applies-when setting refused, and the unanswered setting reported until it is given.

title: Write a flow as ordered steps
steps: On a temporary product, adds a flow with steps on two paths and links them to a view, a command and a requirement.
Runs lathe check, renumbers the step and fulfills the other requirement.
expected_result: Expects the skipped number and the unfulfilled requirements reported, then fixed; a repeated position and another use case's requirement refused.

title: Name records in text without linking them
steps: On a temporary product, sets a requirement's statement naming this product's and another product's IDs, one in a code span.
Shows the record and runs lathe check.
expected_result: Expects the text kept as written, no link added and nothing reported about the IDs.

title: Read each kind's stage and order
steps: On a temporary product, reads the stages and the use-cases kinds from the reference and from lathe check --json.
Declares a product kind in the use-cases stage and reads both again.
expected_result: Expects the five stages in order, the same kind order in both, and the product kind after Lathe's.

title: Model an aggregate's entities and value objects
steps: On a temporary product, adds a root and a child entity, a value object with a field and a constraint, and fields typed by a basic type, the value object and another aggregate.
Runs lathe check, links the child with has_many and checks again.
expected_result: Expects a field with two types refused, the unreached child reported until linked, and the value object in the domain that uses it.

title: Read the reference generated from the schema
steps: On a temporary product, prints the reference with the reference script.
Declares a product kind and a product check and prints it again; tries a kind, a relation and a check with a blank description or explanation.
expected_result: Expects the product's kind and check after Lathe's, and each blank declaration refused.

title: Model commands, events and policies
steps: On a temporary product, adds two commands, an event with a field, the raises and checks links, and a policy hearing the event.
Records the command's change to another aggregate with its reason and runs lathe check.
expected_result: Expects raising another aggregate's event refused, and the recorded exception listed apart with its reason.

title: Write the test plan, one kind per thing tested
steps: On a temporary product, adds an invariant test and a use case test with their run by, and a use case test under an invariant.
Sorts four requirements into two groups with lathe set.
expected_result: Expects the misplaced test refused, both obligations proved, and the groups kept with no lone-child warning.

title: Read how kinds and checks work from where I am
steps: In Chromium, over a copy of this repo's data, opens the record format from the palette, a kind page from the side bar's Kind row, and a check page from a problem's code.
Finds a kind by quick find.
expected_result: Expects each reference page with its title, columns or query and problems.

title: Open a record's data file from the desktop app
manual_reason: Manual because its steps are the operating system's: Finder revealing the file, the chosen editor opening it and the clipboard. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
steps: Run `npm --prefix desktop start` and open a record page. Choose Reveal in Finder: Finder shows the record's data file selected.
Choose Open in editor: the file opens in the editor at the record's line. Choose Copy ID and paste it: the record's ID.
Change the record's title in the editor and save: the page shows the new title within a second or two.
expected_result: It passes when every step behaves as written.

title: Write a standard the code follows
steps: On a temporary product, adds a standard and its rule, links a command handler with meets and adds the rule's test.
Shows the standard and the rule, and runs lathe check.
expected_result: Expects the rule, what meets it and its test shown, and the rule designed, built and proved in Shared coverage.

title: Write the technical records that build the design
steps: On a temporary product, adds a command handler and a repository naming a file, then the file.
Adds the entity's table with a primary key and a unique key naming its invariant.
expected_result: Expects the missing file reported until written, an index key naming an invariant refused, and no implementation gap left.

title: Write the views, endpoints and integrations a flow reaches
steps: On a temporary product, adds an endpoint under a command, a view and an integration with their requirements.
Links the flow step to the view, the integration and the command.
expected_result: Expects the view and integration reported as unused until linked, then no error and both in the step's domain.

title: Merge two branches' data
steps: On a temporary product, in a git repo with the merge driver set up, adds a requirement on each of two branches and merges them.
Changes one row's title on both sides of two new branches and merges them.
expected_result: Expects the first merge to keep both rows sorted and check clean, and the second to stop naming the key, with both versions in the file.

title: Sort a domain's rules by what they do
steps: On a temporary product, adds a constraint, an invariant named on a unique key, and a specification.
Links what the specification reads and the command and query that use it.
expected_result: Expects the unused specification reported until linked, and one of each rule kind in the domain's coverage.

title: Model read models, queries, domain services and terms
steps: On a temporary product, adds a read model with fields, what it reads and its query, then a domain service the query calls and a term.
expected_result: Expects the read model's and service's gaps closed, a query of another domain refused, and the records in the domain.

title: Check the workspace from the command line
steps: On a temporary product, runs lathe check with an unused view, then with --json.
Removes the view and checks again; then breaks a data file and checks.
expected_result: Expects errors, warnings and coverage in order with status 1, status 0 once fixed, and only a data-refused error naming the file and line.

title: Add a check
steps: On a temporary product, adds a check row through lathe add check.
Runs lathe check.
expected_result: Expects the row in data/check.jsonl and its problem reported on the aggregate with no command.

title: Find structural problems and each mistake once
steps: On a temporary product, runs lathe check on stages written at different times: an unused view, a test at a disallowed level, an event by in-process delivery, a recorded exception and a use case with no flow.
Fixes them, then adds a test with its parent's ID to a data file and checks.
expected_result: Expects each reported once where it belongs, then gone, and the bad row as one data-refused error naming its file and line.

title: Add a product's own checks
steps: On a temporary product, adds a house check with the product's product_id and runs lathe check, then fixes what it finds.
Adds a check named like Lathe's, one whose query fails, and a checks key in lathe.config.json.
expected_result: Expects the house check last, its problem gone once fixed, the name refused naming lathe/data/check.jsonl, the failing query an error while others run, and the config key refused.

title: Keep each level of the spec a useful size
steps: On a temporary product, sets low limits with lathe add product_setting and runs lathe check.
Raises the limits, adds a use case and ungroups a lone requirement, then checks again.
expected_result: Expects too many children, too many entities and lone children warned of, then none.

title: Review every problem of a product
steps: In Chromium, over a copy of this repo's data, opens the product's Checks page, adds an unused view to a data file while it is open, opens that problem's record and goes back, and follows the check's code.
Reopens the page as the desktop app with its bridge stood in for.
expected_result: Expects the counts and groups errors first, the new error shown without a reload, the check's page, and the error count sent for the Dock badge.

title: Keep every change to the spec checked
steps: Reads the plugin's hook declaration and runs its guard script with Write, Edit and MultiEdit of a data file, and with other files.
On a temporary product, changes records through lathe.
expected_result: Expects every hand edit of a data file denied pointing at the tools, others passed silently, and a bad write refused.

title: Open the form, save an edit
steps: In Chromium, over a copy of a product, opens a record, chooses Edit, changes a field and saves.
expected_result: Expects the form in place of the content, the record shown changed after the write, and nothing on the page jumping.

title: A day with the desktop app
manual_reason: Manual because it watches what only a person at the screen sees: a flash, the Dock and real windows. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`.
steps: Run `npm --prefix desktop start`. Lathe's repo opens in a window with no white flash, in light and in dark appearance.
Press Cmd+O and choose a folder with neither `lathe.config.json` nor `data/`: a message says what is missing and no window opens. Choose another product's folder: a second window opens.
Choose File › Open Recent › Lathe's folder: the first window comes forward; no third window opens.
Click a link to an outside site in a record: it opens in the system browser, and the window stays on Lathe.
Move and resize the window, quit with Cmd+Q, and run `npm --prefix desktop start` again: the last folder opened reopens in its saved place.
Close every window, then run `ps -A | grep vite`: no dev server the shell started is left.
expected_result: It passes when every step behaves as written.

title: Iterating on Lathe in the desktop app
manual_reason: Manual because it changes files while the shell runs and builds the app. Run it after changing `desktop/scripts/` or the servers.
steps: With the owner's dev server running (`npm --prefix app run dev`), run `npm --prefix desktop run dev`. The terminal says Lathe's folder comes "from shared dev server at http://localhost:5199".
Change a style in `app/src/styles.css`: the window updates without reloading, as the browser does.
Open another product folder with Cmd+O: the terminal says it comes "from own dev server" on a port other than 5199.
Change a record's title in that folder, on its page or with `lathe set`: the page shows the new title within a second or two. Do the same in a window started with `npm --prefix desktop start`.
Change a comment in `desktop/src/menu.ts`: the terminal says it restarts Electron, and the windows come back. Break the file's syntax: the build fails and the running shell stays.

Run `npm --prefix desktop run pack`: `desktop/release/mac-arm64/Lathe.app` (or `mac` on Intel) is built, the log says code signing was skipped, and the app opens from Finder with the chuck icon (right-click › Open the first time, since it is unsigned).
expected_result: It passes when every step behaves as written.

title: The title bar in a real window
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the window's own controls and the system's gestures, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/chrome.ts` or `app/src/shell/DesktopTitleBar.tsx`.
steps: Run `npm --prefix desktop start`. The window has no system title bar; the traffic lights sit centered in Lathe's bar, clear of the back button.
Drag the bar between its controls: the window moves. Double-click it there: the window zooms (or minimizes, if the system's setting says so). Click each control: it acts and the window does not move.
Narrow the window: the command center shortens with an ellipsis and stays centered on the window.
Choose another theme and switch between light and dark: the bar and the window's background follow, with no flash.
expected_result: It passes when every step behaves as written.

title: A native Mac app at the screen
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
steps: Run `npm --prefix desktop run dev`: the Dock shows the icon with a DEV band. Run `npm --prefix desktop run pack` and open the app from `desktop/release/`: the icon is crisp in the Dock, in Finder's list view (16 px) and in Cmd+Tab, in light and in dark appearance.
Open a folder whose checks report errors: the Dock badge shows their number. Fix one: the badge follows. Bring a window with no errors forward: the badge clears.
Right-click the Dock icon: New Window opens the folder picker, and the recent folders are listed (packed app).
Choose Lathe › About Lathe: a small window shows the versions; Source Code and Reference open in the browser. Press Cmd+,: the focused window shows Settings.
On a record, click Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID in its facts, and right-click a record row, a graph node and the page title: the native menu offers the same three and each works.
With the app running, run `open -a Lathe ~/some/product` (packed app) or drag a product folder onto the Dock icon: the running app opens it, and a second time brings its window forward.

Open a new folder: the window shows the shell color and "Opening <product>…" at once, never white. Break a row of one of its data files and reopen the folder: the error page shows the message; fix it and click Retry.

Scroll a long page: the scroll bars float over it. Right-click in quick find: Cut, Copy and Paste. Enter full screen, quit and reopen: the window comes back in full screen, and the title bar's back button sits at the left edge.
Force quit Lathe while it opens its window, then open it again: macOS does not ask to reopen windows.
expected_result: It passes when every step behaves as written. The nav keeps the theme's own color: the system's sidebar material was left out, since it needs a transparent window and nav, which would replace every theme's nav color with the system's gray and give up the shell color that keeps a new window from flashing.

title: See a domain's coverage
steps: On a temporary product, runs lathe check with one requirement done and one not.
Closes the gap with a step and an automated test, and checks again.
expected_result: Expects one coverage line with its gaps and status 0, then the line complete.

title: Count coverage by the meta-model
steps: On a temporary product, with a constraint, an invariant, a requirement and a product obligation kind, adds tests at an allowed and a disallowed level and one not automated yet.
Runs lathe check.
expected_result: Expects a disallowed level to prove nothing, not automated yet counted apart, and one line per kind with the product's kind last.

title: Record how a test is run
steps: On a temporary product, adds an automated, a manual and a not-automated-yet test, the last naming a file not written.
Tries an unknown state and level, an automated test with no file and a manual reason on a test that is not manual.
expected_result: Expects a missing-file warning, the counts by state, and each bad run by refused.

title: Prove the rules of the patterns a domain follows
steps: On a temporary product, writes a pattern's rules, has one domain follow it and another through a use case marking the setting not applicable.
Adds one pattern rule test per owed rule and domain, and runs lathe check.
expected_result: Expects the unfollowed pattern warned of, each rule owed where it applies, every owed rule proved, and an unknown setting refused.

title: Check that each test's file names it
steps: On a temporary product, adds an automated test whose file names a longer ID, then names it.
Adds a manual test and a not-automated-yet test naming a file that does not name them.
expected_result: Expects the error naming the test and file until fixed, and nothing for the other two.

title: See each domain's tests by state
steps: On a temporary product, with one test of each state in one domain, runs lathe check and lathe check --json.
expected_result: Expects the tests line after the domain's coverage, and the same counts in the JSON for every domain.

title: Follow a pattern per domain
steps: On a temporary product, links a domain to a pattern with no settings and a use case to one with a setting, then gives its value.
Declares a product obligation kind and adds a record of it; declares one named like Lathe's table.
expected_result: Expects the missing setting reported until given, each rule owed once for proof only, no requirement asked of the follower, the product kind counted, and the clash refused.

title: Report pattern rule tests that count nowhere and silent manual files
steps: On a temporary product, adds a pattern rule test in a domain that does not follow the pattern, and a manual test whose file does not name it.
Runs lathe check.
expected_result: Expects the pattern rule test reported as an error naming its domain, and the silent manual file a warning.

title: See the domains' coverage and the product's summary
steps: In Chromium, over a copy of this repo's data, opens the product page and reads each domain card, the Summary, the open questions and the problems.
Opens a domain card.
expected_result: Expects the bars, the test counts and the errors to match the served coverage, and the domain page to open.

title: Trace an obligation in the graph
steps: In Chromium, over a copy of this repo's data, focuses a UC requirement in the graph and turns trace mode on.
expected_result: Expects exactly its chain on the canvas and its steps and tests in the side bar.

title: See every obligation kind and test state
steps: In Chromium, over a copy of this repo's data, opens a domain from the product page, reads its coverage groups and opens a gap.
Opens a requirement page and reads its tests.
expected_result: Expects one group per obligation kind with its total, the gap's page, and each test's state.

title: See the patterns a domain follows
steps: In Chromium, over a copy of this repo's data, unfolds a pattern under the domain's Patterns we follow, opens the pattern, then its graph.
expected_result: Expects each rule with its standing, the pattern's settings, rules and followers, and its rules and followers in the graph.

title: See tests by state with each domain's coverage
steps: In Chromium, over a copy of this repo's data, reads each domain card's tests, the Summary's total and a domain's Coverage section.
expected_result: Expects each to match the served counts.

title: See what designs, builds and proves a record
steps: In Chromium, over a copy of this repo's data, searches a domain for a requirement and reads its Traceability, follows its test, goes back and follows a gap's callout.
expected_result: Expects its steps, tests with their state and gap callouts, the test's run by, and the check's page.
